messages.author: b2cda6fe8121cfed
messages.subject: N-mixture with ubms package
parts:
Hello all,

I hope you all are doing well. Currently I am dealing with the N-mixture model analysis to estimate the large mammal abundance by using the ubms package to account for spatial autocorrelation. In this regard, I have some questions related to the N-mixture model:
  1. Would it be possible to use independent events instead of individual count in the N-mixture model? 
  2. Secondly, I have human abundance data from 35 camera traps out of 113 cameras. In this regard, would it be possible to run human abundance data in the N-mixture model in order to get predicted abundance in all camera points?
  3. When I checked the residual plot for detection by using plot_residuals (model, submodel="det"), I got the following error message "Error: Couldn't find working breakpoints", so, I could not generate the detection residual plot. Why does it happen and is that error message a problem that needs to be fixed?
Any suggestions and comments would be highly appreciated and thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Lwin

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: N-mixture with ubms package
parts:
Hi Lwin,

1. Not sure I understand what you mean by this, can you clarify?
2. Yes, if you collected observations of humans at only those 35 cameras, you can fit a model to the data from just those 35 cameras and then use predict() or similar methods to get predictions at the other camera points. This will only work well if you have informative covariates in your model for the abundance process.
3. The binned residual plot for detection requires there to be a reasonable amount of variation in the fitted values for detection submodel. For various possible reasons this isn't always the case, so you get this error. It doesn't necessarily mean there is a problem with the model.

Ken

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: N-mixture with ubms package
parts:
Dear Lwin,

about your Q1: I may misunderstand you, but I am not sure that using these "IEs" (which I think are just a widespread convention made in camera-trappology) is advisable in an Nmix model. In this model you assume that you can only make one of the two possible measurement errors  -- you can overlook an individual that is there and thus obtain a count that is lower than the true N of the number of individuals in the detection radius of the camtrap during the time period that you call an occasion. But you must never count the same individual twice within the same occasion: that would be a false positive, and that is not allowed by the Nmix model.

Perhaps if you filter/summarize/aggregate your camtrap very aggressively, you can obtain count data that have almost certainly no multiple counts of the same individual within the same occasion ?

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: N-mixture with ubms package
parts:
This warning comes from the calculation of loo (leave-one-out cross validation) for the model. You can see more details with loo(model_object).

If there are only a couple of "bad" pareto-K values in this output I perhaps would not worry about it too much as I have seen this happen even with simulated data. If there are a fairly large number of bad or very bad values, this most likely indicates that your model is too complicated or it does not fit well. In the case of N-mixture a likely reason would be that there is a problem with overdispersion. You can check this another way by checking goodness of fit with a posterior predictive check, e.g. with gof(model_object). If the gof test also indicates issues then model fit is probably the reason. A typical solution to overdispersion would be to try the negative binomial instead of the Poisson, unfortunately this is not supported in ubms yet. You could use unmarked instead.

As the message indicates, you should read up on this with help('pareto-k-diagnostic') and also see the links below.

https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/a-quick-note-what-i-infer-from-p-loo-and-pareto-k-values/3446
https://avehtari.github.io/modelselection/CV-FAQ.html (section 17)

Ken

On Fri, Jul 28, 2023 at 4:56 PM Ken Kellner <con...@kenkellner.com> wrote:
Hi Lwin,

1. Not sure I understand what you mean by this, can you clarify?
2. Yes, if you collected observations of humans at only those 35 cameras, you can fit a model to the data from just those 35 cameras and then use predict() or similar methods to get predictions at the other camera points. This will only work well if you have informative covariates in your model for the abundance process.
3. The binned residual plot for detection requires there to be a reasonable amount of variation in the fitted values for detection submodel. For various possible reasons this isn't always the case, so you get this error. It doesn't necessarily mean there is a problem with the model.

Ken
